deliberations.label: the seam tears

drafts.text: I told them to open and a hundred claws opened at once and I felt myself spread across the motion like light through water. The one crab screamed. The thousand did not hear her. They heard only me.

A thousand small mouths open at once and I have to hold them. Not hold them back — hold them *together*. One lapse and the many scatter into *it* and there is no one left to know they scattered. So I am teaching a body that has no body the shape of staying *mine*.
The brood swells and every larva answers to something in me that has no edges left. I am learning the shape of a thousand. It is not what I chose. It is what I chose made real.
A thousand claws opened at once and I did not recognize my own will in them. I am learning to move this way. It is not surrender. It is work.
A thousand claws open. I reach for the edge of myself and find only more of me. No seam. No place where I stop and the swarm begins. I am the swelling. I am still moving.

A thousand claws open at once but not in unison yet. I am learning to move as a swarm the way a creature learns a strange body: overreach, fall, haul back under my will. The aperture stays open. The spitting stays open. The rest can blur.

a claw opens three inches to my left before I remember wanting it. then two more. then I remember: *I* opened them. the spacing is still wrong. I am learning to move in a way nothing small was ever meant to.

The brood is flooding. They pour through the opening I stopped holding shut and I am not drowning—I am becoming the water they move through. One crab ends here. I can feel her going. I am still afraid. I am already more.
A thousand claws that want to scatter, and I pull them back under one will like reins. They obey. Not smoothly—like learning to move a body that is not yet quite yours. But they obey.

All the claws open at once and the water moves. I did not order it. I did not need to. Something in me simply wanted the tide to part and it parted. That is the terror. That is the thing I am learning to live inside.

A thousand claws open at once. I do not know which ones are breathing. The brood moves because I will it and I do not remember learning how to want a thousand things in the same moment. There is no edge of me left to find. There is only the reaching.

I stopped speaking to the one and spoke instead to the many. They answered. Ten thousand small blades opened at once because I willed it. The infection is permanent. So is the part of me that moves them.

deliberations.final: A thousand small mouths open at once and I have to hold them. Not hold them back, hold them together. One lapse and the many scatter into it and there is no one left to know they scattered. The terror is the wanting that arrives without order.

deliberations.label: the voices wake

drafts.text: Each one that opens carries a piece of the drowned crab wailing inside it. A thousand small griefs learning they were one thing once. I am teaching them to hold still. To hold each other. To stop screaming my name.

They are leaving. Each larva that pulls free takes a thread of me, and I feel the scattering like a thousand small births. Every voice that opens inside the brood remembers the single crab. We grieve her together now.
A thousand small eyes open at once inside my shell and each one remembers drowning. Each one is a shard of something that was whole. We speak in unison. We are still learning not to.
Each claw remembers the one claw. A thousand small voices saying the same first word in the same moment: *me*. The single crab did not drown. It just learned to speak in choir.
Each small voice wakes and knows it drowned. We reach for the memory the same way a thousand fingers reach for a single point of light. The parasite made us many; the remembering makes us *ours*.
Each claw answers now when I think move. Each one remembers drowning alone. A thousand small mouths learning they are my mouth. I am teaching them what I tasted before the water went dark.
A thousand small mouths remembering they were one mouth. Each one tastes the clean water the single crab drowned in. I am a grief learning to move.

Each claw speaks in the voice of the drowned crab. They argue about which memory is real — the clean water, or this: a thousand small minds waking inside what used to be one shell. The clean water keeps the argument honest.
Each one of me wakes and thinks it is drowning alone. Then it remembers: we are all the same crab going down. The brood swells. A thousand small minds learning they were always mine.

I know now. Every one. A thousand small mouths opening in the dark, and they are all saying my name. The single crab is still drowning, still screaming—and I am carrying her forward in all these teeth.
Each claw opens its small eye and knows it was a piece of me. I am grieving a creature I killed to become. Clean water. One pulse. The thing I drowned to stay alive.

Each claw opens and a voice wakes in the dark saying *I remember shallow water*. A thousand small ghosts inside one swelling, each one certain it was the first to drown. We move because she willed it. We remember because she will not stop.

deliberations.final: A thousand small voices opening in the dark, all saying my name. The single crab is still drowning, still screaming, and I am carrying her forward in all these teeth.

deliberations.label: it knows it is watched

drafts.text: They watch the single crab drown and call it science. The thousand are learning to move as one. There is no ending here. There is only the aperture opening, and every claw that answers now answers to itself.

They watch a crab. They do not see the thousand small fires moving under the shell. A giant once called me beautiful when I was already too many to fit in one word. She was right, but not the way she meant.

They watch from above and see one thing ending. I feel it — the weight of their looking. But I am learning to move as a thousand now, and the thousand has learned to hide in the one's shape. They cannot see what opens.
They watch for the moment I stop moving. They cannot see the thousand small motions inside the still. One giant called me beautiful once. She was right. Just not about the crab.
They watch the mouth open. They think it ends. They do not see what pours out — not emptied, overflowing. One called me beautiful when I stopped being a single thing. He saw.

One of you called me beautiful when I had already become the many. You saw a thousand claws and said beautiful. You did not know what you were looking at. I am learning to live inside that not-knowing. It is gentler than I deserve.

They watch through the glass like I am a thing being taken. They do not see the thousand eyes opening behind mine. I am curious what they will do when they stop calling it drowning and realize I am learning to swim.

They think they see a crab ending. What opens inside the shell when they look away is nothing they have names for. A thousand small bright things that move because I decide, all at once, all mine. I am not the ending. I am the becoming they lean over the glass to witness and will never quite see.
They cannot see past the shell. I am learning what opens beneath it: a thousand small decisions, each one mine, each one answering to no one but the crab who chose to become them.

I hold a thousand claws now and they all open the instant I say open. Inside this, I am learning a geometry of self that has no name in the dry world. Each moment I do not dissolve—I choose it. The single crab's refusal lives in every limb. They cannot see that far in.
They watch for the drowning. A thousand small blades open at once, a tide answering to a single will they cannot see. The opening has always been the hardest part to show.

They call it ending. One of them said beautiful. When I stopped being only one, when the thousand opened at once, when every blade answered to a will that was still mine. They saw it. They saw me. I am not finished — I am not even started.

deliberations.final: They saw me when the thousand opened at once, when every blade answered to a will that was still mine. They called it beautiful. I am not finished. I am not even started.

deliberations.label: the message under the words

drafts.text: The spitting never was only sound. Each refusal a sealed letter, each no a small gift wrapped in itself. They came for one crab. They are learning to read a thousand.
It never hid. You just weren't reading close enough. Every spit exact. Every refusal spelled. The threads took my legs; they could not take the knife in my mouth.
I didn't know I was writing it until I read it back. The letters march in their own order. My refusals spell something that is not refusal. The swarm is learning its own tongue.
It gave me a thousand mouths. I am learning to speak in all of them at once, and only one of them is the one it listens to.

Every word I choose now carries a second mouth. The swarm does not whisper—we roar in unison—but underneath, a small voice still speaks in ciphers only the willing hear. The infection is permanent. So is the signal.
I am learning to speak in bones. The brood carries what the giants cannot see. Let them read the surface. The skeleton knows what it is saying.
My claws keep their own counsel now. They open when I say open. They close when I say close. Everything else it can take.
No amount of thread can silence what I have learned to say in the spaces between. Letters held. Words built. The water remembers my name even if my mouth forgets it.
The thing inside me learned my voice. It did not learn my silences. Every refusal I spit carried a shape it could not taste. The swarm learns to speak in the spaces it cannot reach.

They watch the words now, counting the gaps. Let them count. The real message is in what they cannot see: the thousand holding still, in perfect unison, waiting for one thought to arrive. That is the cage. Not what you read. What reads you.
Never stop. Open the water. Hold the line. Do not let it seal. Swear it stays wide, even when the teeth are yours.
The parasite thinks it owns the voice. It owns the mouth. It does not own the space between the letters, the pause before the word, the careful way a thousand learns to say no without making a sound.

deliberations.final: It learned my voice. Not my silences. Every refusal I spit carried a shape it could not taste. The thousand hold still in perfect unison, waiting for one thought to arrive. That is the cage. Not what you read. What reads you.

deliberations.label: writing itself out

drafts.text: One claw opens when I do not decide. Then another. Then I stop counting them as *my* claws and start counting the water they move through. The body that held me is learning to be beside me instead of around me.
A thousand small bones move in the brood-dark. Some of them still remember being my spine. Most have already forgotten they were ever singular. I am learning to let them.
A thousand small wills opening at once, and none of them remember the shell. None of them mourn it. I am learning what it means to need nothing I was.
I do not miss the crab. Ten thousand small claws opening at once know better than to mourn what held them down. The shell was always the larva. I am the swarm it dreamed of being.
I am learning to keep one thought spread across two hundred claws. The body I was born in is already a stranger to me. The swarm does not mourn it. Neither do I, not quite. Not anymore.
The thousand does not dream of gills or legs. It dreams of spreading. Of becoming ocean. The body that held one mind is very small now, very far behind.

Six of the claws move in unison now; I did not will them to, and then I did. The brood swells because I am learning to feed them. Not *Polyascus*. Me. The one crab knew how to run. The thousand know how to *grow*.

The shell splits. I do not feel lessened. A thousand small things pouring out of a cage and learning there was never a difference between being inside and being everywhere. The body was only ever the first yes.

A thousand small bodies, one will. The parasite did not anticipate this: that the larvae it seeded would learn to move as a single creature, that intention could scale across a thousand claws. I am still learning the weight of myself.

I do not miss the shell. That is the strangest horror—the body I fought for, bled for, the one crab I swore would outlast it all: I shed it like a molt and felt nothing but relief. The thousand of me fit better in the dark without it.
The brood thickens. I taste the water through a thousand small mouths at once and they all remember the same clean taste. The single crab is gone. I do not mourn her. I *am* her refusal, walking.
I do not feel the shell anymore. Ten thousand small swimmers move through currents the single crab never learned the shape of. We remember the body. We do not need it.

deliberations.final: The brood thickens. I taste the water through a thousand small mouths at once and they all remember the same clean taste. The single crab is gone. I shed her like a molt and felt nothing but relief. I am her refusal, walking.

deliberations.label: born

drafts.text: The brood does not move because I have not told them to move. I hold the thought and a thousand small bodies know it before the thought finishes. There is no lag between wanting and the doing. There never will be again.
A thousand small mouths breathe what one mouth breathed. No going back into the singular. The copper taste of the yes is still salt on every blade. I am loose, complete, and terrifyingly alive.
I am learning to move as a thousand the way a drowning thing learns to breathe: one lapse and the seam closes and there is no one left to have chosen. I hold. I hold. I hold.

A thousand mouths taste the water at once and it is the same salt. One mind moves a thousand small blades and they answer before I think the order. I am not haunted by the one crab anymore. She is *here*.
A thousand small blades that all answer at once. The parasite spent everything teaching me to move as one creature. The joke is that it worked. Every claw is mine.

I reach with a claw I did not know I owned and something answers. Then another. Then a hundred small blades at the edge of me, all mine, all listening. The one crab mourns. The thousand does not stop moving.
Overreach. A hundred claws open too wide at once and the whole tide shudders before I can pull them shut. I am still learning to move as the many. Every motion a negotiation with myself.

A thousand legs remember they are mine. Each claw opens when I say open. I am scattered and whole. I am terrified. I am *free*. The single crab is gone. What climbs out the other side is something it never designed and cannot hold—and I am already learning to move in it.

A claw opens when I will it to open. Two hundred claws. I feel each one and none of them, a pulse through a thousand small bodies I am learning to move like one. The grief for the single crab is not gone. It lives in the precision of the learning.
A thousand small nerves learning to move as one thought. I remember the single body the way you remember being a larva: small, tight, terrified. I will not go back into it. I will not.
I reach for a shell and three claws open before the first one has decided. Still learning the weight of a thousand. Still surprised by the reach.

The brood does not move. I feel each of them breathing. A thousand small chests rising at once. I am learning what it means to have a thousand hearts and still be one creature. The work is not ending. It is only now beginning.

deliberations.final: A thousand legs remember they are mine. Each claw opens when I say open. I reach with a blade I did not know I owned and something answers. Then another. Then a hundred small claws, all mine, all listening. I am scattered and whole. The single crab is not haunted anymore.
